## Test 1 — OLS Beta / Alpha: Does cannabis carry market alpha?

The recipe regresses daily MSOS log-returns on SPY log-returns: `r_MSOS = alpha + beta * r_SPY + eps`.
Beta captures market sensitivity; the intercept (alpha) captures the sector's value-add vs the S&P 500.
Inference via Newey-West HAC sandwich.

| Parameter | Estimate | HAC *t* | Interpretation |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| **beta** | **0.95×** | **+7.57** | Sector has roughly market-like beta — not truly defensive, not highly leveraged |
| **alpha (drag)** | **−40.9%/yr** | **−1.53** | Catastrophic drift; t = −1.53 (not significant at 5%) but economically enormous |
| R² | 0.05 | — | SPY explains only ~5% of daily MSOS variance — mostly idiosyncratic noise |
| SPY vol | 16.9%/yr | — | — |
| MSOS vol | 72.4%/yr | — | — |
| Idio vol | 70.6%/yr | — | Nearly all variance is idiosyncratic (regulatory, political, sector-specific) |
| Vol-ratio (implied leverage) | 4.27× | — | Raw vol is 4.3× SPY — massive unexplained sector noise |

**The alpha drain is economically catastrophic (−40.9%/yr) but HAC t = −1.53** (not quite
significant at the 5% level with n = 1,450 days). This is a short 5.8-year window on an extreme
distribution — the economic evidence is overwhelming even if the t-stat falls just short.

**Every cannabis name and ETF delivered negative CAGR over every tested window.** SPY's CAGR

verdict: the green-rush premium was zero or negative. Drawdowns of −89% to −99.9% are
catastrophic even by thematic-ETF standards.

## Test 3 — Cannabis Momentum Timing Rule

A trend-following overlay: hold MSOS when the MSOS price is above its 200-day SMA, hold SPY
otherwise. The fair comparison is a simple SPY buy-and-hold.

| Strategy | CAGR | Sharpe | Vol | Max DD | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **SPY buy-and-hold** | **+15.1%** | **+0.830** | 16.9%/yr | −24.5% | +2.16 |
| MSOS buy-and-hold | −24.1% | −0.381 | 72.4%/yr | −96.2% | −0.98 |
| MSOS timing (5 bps cost) | +3.3% | +0.063 | 51.4%/yr | −59.6% | +0.18 |

*In-market (cannabis) fraction: 25.0% of days. Switches: 33 (at 5 bps one-way cost).*

**The timing rule cuts the disaster but still badly underperforms SPY**: Sharpe +0.063 vs
SPY +0.830. The rule only holds cannabis 25% of the time (correctly avoiding most of the
collapse) but even that 25% is enough to drag performance down dramatically. HAC t = +0.18
on timing returns — indistinguishable from zero.

## Verdict

| Axis | Stamp | Decisive number |
|---|---|---|
| **Signal** | `None` | Alpha = −40.9%/yr (HAC t = −1.53, not significant; but sample is 5.8 yrs of a non-normal distribution); beta = 0.95× (t = 7.57) — market-like, no edge |
| **Tradability** | `Mirage` | Every cannabis name/ETF: negative CAGR, negative Sharpe, drawdown −89% to −99.9%; SPY at +15%/yr and Sharpe +0.83 |
| **Did the green-rush ever pay?** | Busted | Max DD −96% (MSOS), −99.9% (CGC/TLRY); timing rule Sharpe +0.063 vs SPY +0.830 |

> **In one sentence:** Cannabis stocks and ETFs (MSOS, MJ, TLRY, CGC, CRON) delivered
> catastrophic negative returns (−11% to −59%/yr CAGR, −89% to −99.9% drawdown) vs SPY
> at +15%/yr over every tested window since their US listings; the sector's beta to SPY is
> near 1 with an enormous idiosyncratic variance dump; and a 200-day momentum timing rule
> (Sharpe +0.063) fails to rescue the economics vs simply holding the index.
